text:
Aisha: FYI - overnight canary failing attestation. cosign returns "key disabled" when trying to sign image: base-slim:sha256:ff11.
Ben: ugh, we rotated the cosign key last night as part of the key hygiene sweep. I thought we kept the old key active for 48h grace.
Carlos: looks like the old key was disabled rather than scheduled for automatic deletion. Did the rotation script call `gcloud kms keys disable`?
Ben: checking logs... yes, rotation job invoked `--state=DISABLED` by mistake on cosign-key. My bad, typo in the rotation workflow.
Lin: that would explain the immediate signing failures. Can we re-enable the key? What's the policy on re-enabling vs emergency rotation?
Oncall: re-enable is allowed if the key hasn't been scheduled for destroy; re-enable will restore signing as long as key material is intact. But any IAM binding changes after disable may complicate audit trails. We have to record the change.
Aisha: we need a short mitigation: 1) re-enable cosign-key 2) route canary to alternate ephemeral key for any new pushes 3) create an audit entry linking the RBAC change + rotation job.
Carlos: doing step 2 now. I'll create a temp-key `cosign-ephemeral-2026` in the same ring and update the attestor config for pods with label `canary=true`. Pushing helm patch in ~15m.
sec-ci-bot: CI_SCAN: base-slim:ff11 - ATTESTATION_FAILED - cosign: signing error: key disabled by admin. See https://ci.internal/scans/ff11
Ben: step 1: I'm going to re-enable the key. Running: 

```
# re-enable key (gcloud)
gcloud kms keys versions restore \ 
  --location=global --keyring=signer --key=cosign-key --version=1
```
Ben: note - if version restore fails we'll need to accept ephemeral key and rotate consumers.
Lin: before you re-enable, ensure the audit export sink has been recording `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.sign` events. We had an issue last quarter where the sink SA lost BigQuery permissions and events were dropped.
Aisha: good call. Carlos, can you confirm audit sink health?
Carlos: checking sink: `audit-sinks/kms-audit` shows last delivery 10m ago, but there was an error 2h ago: BigQuery writer SA `sink-writer@project` lacked `roles/bigquery.dataEditor`. Opening OPS ticket OPS-4832 to restore sink perms.
Oncall: OPS-4832 received. We'll prioritize. If sink is down, re-enabling key still okay but document the timeline and remediate sink ASAP.
Ben: re-enable command succeeded, signature tests still fail though — maybe IAM binding for service account got removed in the RBAC prune. Error now: `permission denied: cloudkms.cryptoKeys.sign`
Aisha: which principal? cosign-svc@redwood-prod. Did the RBAC cleanup remove `roles/cloudkms.signerVerifier`?
Ben: checking git... PR #842 removed several roles and added least-privilege rules. It did remove `signerVerifier` from `serviceAccounts/*cosign*` in prod due to an overly broad grep. I'll re-add binding with a conditional.
Lin: suggest adding a conditional binding: only allow sign from infra CIDR and when request contains `x-cosign-workflow: true` attribute. Example IAM condition snippet: 

```
{
  "role": "roles/cloudkms.signerVerifier",
  "members": ["serviceAccount:cosign-svc@redwood-prod"],
  "condition": {
    "title": "cosign-allowed",
    "expression": "request.auth.claims.aud == 'cosign' && request.ip == '10.0.0.0/16'"
  }
}
```
Carlos: okay I'll prepare a minimal RBAC patch and include a terraform plan guard. PR coming shortly.
Aisha: also add a CI check that runs `gcloud iam policies get-iam-policy` for cosign-key and fails if signer binding missing. We need to prevent accidental removals.
sec-ci-bot: SUGGESTION: add terraform test that queries `google_kms_crypto_key_iam_binding` and validates known members. See docs at internal://devops/iam-tests
Ben: created PR #849 to re-add binding with condition. Linking OPS-4832 for sink fix.
Oncall: schedule change window for full key rotation if needed. Tentative: 03:30 UTC. I'll coordinate with infra and release teams.
Aisha: secondary action: vuln scan flagged library `libnet-xs` with advisory RD-2026-47 in the base image, not directly related to signing but track it as SEC-2920. Carlos, please add to vuln board.
Carlos: SEC-2920 created and assigned to Lin for impact + mitigation.
Lin: quick binary diff shows library present but not used by runtime paths. ETA for full vetting 4h. If low we proceed with canary after binder fix.
Aisha: thanks. Final ask: once RBAC/Key is restored, run end-to-end attestation smoke: local cosign sign -> verify in CI -> canary rollout. Post results here.
Ben: will run smoke tests and post logs. If anything fails, we'll fall back to ephemeral key for canaries until full audit sink confirmed.
sec-ci-bot: ACTION: DEPLOY_HOLD set for canary/base-slim until attestation smoke passes.
Aisha: summary: Ben re-enabled key (done), Carlos creating ephemeral key + helm patch (in progress), Carlos opened OPS-4832 for audit sink, Ben opened PR #849 to re-add IAM binding with condition, Lin vetting RD-2026-47 (4h). Reconvene here after smoke tests. :white_check_mark:
